elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The carve-out applies only to a “financially responsible affiliate,” not to affiliates generally.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause permits assignment to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, but omits acquisition successors.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without Customer consent to a financially responsible affiliate or, on notice, to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The other party’s required approval, including Customer approval of a Vendor assignment, “shall not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause grants no termination right arising from Customer’s change of control.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The mutual exception permits either party to assign to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment exception is expressly conditioned on written notice.
Assignments to financially responsible affiliates also require no consent, even though they are not successor assignments.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments requiring approval, the clause states that approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.
